sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Sign-in screen imports
sections.what: Brings in the state helper, the sign-in library, the routing and link tools, and a trophy icon. The file is marked to run in the browser.
sections.why: Likely reason: the form must respond to typing and clicks, so it runs in the browser.

sections.name: LoginPage (part 1)
sections.title: Submitting and handling the result
sections.what: When the form is sent, it asks the sign-in service to check the email and password without an automatic redirect. A failure shows an error, with rate limit wording passed through and other failures shown as invalid credentials. A success sends the user to the requested page on this site, or to the crews page.
sections.why: The code comment says the redirect must stay on this site, which blocks sending users to other sites. Likely reason for the error handling: it shows a lockout message while hiding other details.
sections.watch_out: The rate limit message appears only if the server's text contains the words too many, so a change to the server message would show the generic error instead.

sections.name: LoginPage (part 2)
sections.title: Form fields and sign-in button
sections.what: Draws the Welcome Back card with a trophy icon, the email and password fields (both required), and the Sign In button. The button is disabled and shows a spinner while the request runs. A link leads to the registration page.
sections.why: Likely reason: the button is disabled while loading to stop duplicate submissions.
sections.watch_out: The fields are required only in the browser, so the server must still check credentials, and that check lives outside this file.

summary: The sign-in form where an existing user enters email and password and is sent on to the page they wanted.
purpose: Lets an existing user sign in.
why: Private pages such as the notebook and season file need a signed-in user, so this is the entry point.
how: Steps in order: the form shows email and password fields. On submit, it asks the sign-in service to check the credentials without an automatic redirect. If the service returns an error, it shows the message if it mentions too many attempts, or a generic invalid credentials message otherwise. If sign-in works, it reads the requested page from the address, accepts it only if it is a path on this site, and otherwise uses the crews page. Then it refreshes the page state.
inputs: The typed email and password, and the callbackUrl value in the address.
outputs: A signed-in session on success, an error message on failure, and a move to the next page.
risks: The rate limit message appears only if the server's error text contains the words too many. The redirect check is the only guard against sending users to another site. The loading spinner is not cleared after a successful sign-in, so the page depends on navigation happening.
debug: If the wrong error shows, check the text the sign-in service returns. If sign-in works but the user lands on the wrong page, check the callbackUrl value. If the button spins forever, check whether navigation happened after sign-in.
